newsitem.title: USA: S&P AFFIRMS LINCOLN NATIONAL, CIGNA RATINGS.
newsitem.headline: S&P AFFIRMS LINCOLN NATIONAL, CIGNA RATINGS.

text.p: NEW YORK, July 28 - Standard & Poor's today has affirmed its ratings of Lincoln National Corp. (LNC) and affiliated entities (see list below).
Also, Standard & Poor's has affirmed its ratings of CIGNA Corp. (CIGNA; see list) and the ratings of primary subsidiary, Connecticut General Life Insurance Co.

The affirmations follow the announcement that LNC will purchase the life insurance (excluding corporate-owned life insurance) and annuity operations of CIGNA Corp. for $1.4 billion in a transaction expected to close within six months. This transaction will allow both companies to become more focused on core operations, LNC's being life insurance, annuity, and asset management and CIGNA's being employer and employee focused insurance, especially health care, retirement services, and group life.

Standard & Poor's believes that the purchase of CIGNA's life insurance business by LNC brings more balance to the LNC revenue and earnings base of what was primarily an annuity company, and presents opportunities for cost savings.
The following are other major rating factors underlying the LNC ratings:
-- A long-time, dominant position in the annuity marketplace. In 1996, the company had about $4.0 billion in annuity deposits and over $30 billion in annuity assets under management.
Over the past few years, Lincoln National Life (LNL) has been emphasizing variable annuities, with the mix of in-force business split evenly between fixed and variable.
-- Outstanding well diversified business position in the life reinsurance business.
-- Capitalization, on a consolidated basis, is considered appropriate for the rating level, with a Standard & Poor's capital adequacy ratio of approximately 150% pro forma.
Expectations for Lincoln National:
-- The capital adequacy ratio will remain at or above the 150% level, reflecting excellent risk-based capital.
-- The current level of liquidity resources, considered good by Standard & Poor's, will be maintained.
-- Annual statutory net operating income will average 90-100 basis points return on assets.
-- Debt leverage at LNC will remain below 20%, with coverage ratios above 6 times.
-- Life insurance sales will increase at a modest level above industry in 1998 after a transition year in 1996.

Standard & Poor's expects CIGNA will use the proceeds from this transaction to fund common share repurchase, acquisitions, and internal growth without significantly altering its existing capital structure.
With the divestiture of its individual life and annuity business, Standard & Poor's believes the overall business of CIGNA is somewhat less diversified and will skew more towards health care.
Pro forma with this transaction, operating income from health care is 53% of total operating income.
This ratio is expected to further increase in the next several years, as Standard & Poor's believes CIGNA will continue to expand its health care business through internal growth and acquisitions.
In addition, another 15% of CIGNA's operating income is from property casualty insurance.
Standard & Poor's views the health care and property casualty insurance businesses as more volatile than the individual life, annuity, and retirement benefits businesses.
CIGNA's ratings continue to reflect its good business diversification, an excellent earnings history, conservative debt-to-capital ratios, strong liquidity, and above average financial flexibility.

In 1997's first quarter, operating income increased 18.7% from the comparable period in 1996, reflecting continued improvement in all segments, including property and casualty. CIGNA's capitalization continued to be conservative.
Total debt to capital of 16% at Dec. 31, 1996 is low, but has increased in 1997's second quarter to about 24% because it has issued debt to finance the Healthsource acquisition.
Total debt to capital is expected to remain at 25% or below in the foreseeable future, and interest coverage is expected to remain excellent, at about 9 times.
OUTLOOK (LNC): Negative.
The outlook on the debt rating of LNC remains negative, reflecting the challenges that the company faces in its core life insurance and disability lines.
The life insurance segment faces the task of the integration of two different distribution forces serving disparate markets.
The disability income line of business last week had its third major reserve strengthening action since 1993.
OUTLOOK (CIGNA): Negative.

CIGNA's ratings outlook remains negative, in connection with its acquisition of Healthsource. Healthsource has experienced increased competition in its core markets and higher-than-expected health care costs, exacerbated by operational issues related to premium pricing and provider contracts in the markets that Healthsource has entered recently.
If CIGNA is unsuccessful in assimilating Healthsource's operations to generate the desired cost savings, it will have adverse effects on CIGNA's prospective earnings performance. RATINGS AFFIRMED
